quizzes.title: UCC Background: MCQ Practice
quizzes.passage:
Gujarat has passed the Uniform Civil Code Bill 2026, becoming the second state after Uttarakhand to enact such a code. A uniform civil code is often described as a progressive goal for a secular nation, but its implementation has never been simple. The need for a uniform law was first considered during the colonial period, and the question has been debated in different forms ever since.

Personal laws govern matters such as marriage, divorce and succession, and the Gujarat code aims to replace diverse religious personal laws on these matters. The Constitution contains a provision that urges the state to establish a uniform civil code for all citizens. Historically, the adoption of such a code has been controversial.

The Law Commission has revived the idea in recent years and has gathered public views on it. Uttarakhand's code incorporates elements from existing laws but leaves out certain concepts found in other personal laws. The Supreme Court has also called for implementing a uniform code in many cases.

The Gujarat law also seeks to ensure equal inheritance rights for sons and daughters, and its monogamy rule prohibits polygamy and bigamy. The booklet notes that the code is a progressive reform, but that it risks deepening societal divisions in the context of upcoming elections, where justice should take precedence over the pursuit of uniformity.

questions.q: Under which Article does the Constitution urge the state to establish a uniform civil code?
questions.explanation: Article 44 urges the state to establish a uniform civil code for all citizens.

questions.q: In 1948, who was chosen to chair the sub-committee developing the Hindu Code Bill?
questions.explanation: Nehru chose Dr. B. R. Ambedkar in 1948 to chair the sub-committee.

questions.q: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 codified intestate succession among which communities?
questions.explanation: The Act codified intestate succession among Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The provision urging a uniform civil code can be enforced by courts against the state.
Reason (R): That provision is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy, which are not enforceable.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The provision is part of the non-enforceable DPSP, so A is false and R is true.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Lex Loci Report   ->   A. 1956
II. B N Rau Committee   ->   B. 1840
III. Hindu Succession Act   ->   C. 1948
IV. Sub-committee for the Hindu Code Bill   ->   D. 1941
questions.explanation: The Lex Loci Report is 1840, the B N Rau Committee 1941, the Hindu Succession Act 1956 and the Hindu Code sub-committee 1948.

questions.q:
I. The principle underlying a UCC is that laws should be gender-neutral and religion-neutral.
II. Personal laws on marriage, divorce and succession are placed in the Concurrent List.
III. The B N Rau Committee was formed by the Constituent Assembly in 1941.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The B N Rau Committee was formed by the colonial government, not the Constituent Assembly.

questions.q:
I. Article 44 is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy.
II. Personal laws on marriage, divorce and succession fall under the Concurrent List.
III. The principle of the UCC is that laws should be religion-based.
Which option gives the number of correct statements above?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III reverses its principle of religion-neutral laws.

questions.q: Which report of 1840 first considered the need for a uniform law in India?
questions.explanation: The Lex Loci Report of 1840 first considered the need for a uniform law.

questions.q: In which year did the colonial government form the B N Rau Committee?
questions.explanation: The colonial government formed the B N Rau Committee in 1941 to examine common Hindu laws.

questions.q: How many Bills constituted the Hindu Code Bills?
questions.explanation: Four Bills constituted the Hindu Code: the Hindu Marriage Act 1955 and three Acts of 1956.

questions.q: The principle underlying a UCC is that laws should be religion-neutral and which other term?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that UCC laws should be gender-neutral and religion-neutral.

questions.q: Personal laws on marriage, divorce and succession are placed under which list of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Personal laws on marriage, divorce and succession are under the Concurrent List.

questions.q: Article 44 is part of which constitutional category that is not enforceable?
questions.explanation: Article 44 is part of the DPSP, which is not enforceable.

questions.q: In which year was the Hindu Succession Act adopted to codify intestate succession?
questions.explanation: The Hindu Succession Act was adopted in 1956 to codify intestate succession among Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs.

quizzes.title: UCC Arguments: MCQ Practice
quizzes.passage:
Supporters present the Uniform Civil Code as a progressive goal, and the Gujarat Bill is part of that case. The Gujarat law seeks to replace diverse personal laws on marriage, divorce and inheritance with a single civil framework that applies across the state. The Gujarat Bill follows Uttarakhand, which was the first state after pre-Independence Goa to adopt such a code.

The case for the code rests on the idea that personal laws should not lead to unequal treatment of citizens in family life. Supporters also say the code can address unfair treatment within families, and that a common law would let citizens rely on the same rules in family matters, whatever their background.

The Central Government has described different property and matrimonial laws for different communities as a threat to the nation's unity, and it has favoured a common code. The Constitution also contains a provision that urges the state to work towards such a code, so the idea has a constitutional basis.

Critics, however, have raised concerns about the code's effect on individual freedoms in matters of faith. The booklet notes that the subject carries risks in the context of upcoming elections, and it argues that justice should come before uniformity.

questions.q: Critics argue that a UCC goes against the right to freedom of religion guaranteed under which Articles?
questions.explanation: Critics say the UCC is against the freedom of religion guaranteed under Articles 25-28.

questions.q: Critics say a UCC might not adequately accommodate what of different communities?
questions.explanation: The booklet notes that a UCC might not accommodate the unique customs and sensitivities of different communities.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Critics argue that implementation of a UCC could be politically exploited.
Reason (R): Supporters argue that a UCC promotes gender equality.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements appear in the booklet, but the gender equality objective does not explain the political exploitation concern.

questions.q: The UCC is presented as a way to align the law with which feature of the Indian state?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists alignment with the secular nature of the Indian state as an objective.

questions.q: The UCC is presented as a way to reform which kind of practices?
questions.explanation: Reforming outdated and regressive practices is listed as an objective of the UCC.

questions.q:
I. The UCC is presented as a means to eliminate discriminatory practices against women.
II. Critics note that some civil laws are inseparably connected with religious beliefs and practices.
III. The UCC is expected to fully accommodate the unique customs of every community.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement III reverses the concern that a UCC might not accommodate unique customs.

questions.q:
I. Supporters see the UCC as a step towards gender equality.
II. Critics fear that the UCC could be politically exploited.
III. The UCC is presented as a means to promote a religion-specific civil code.
Which option gives the number of correct statements above?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II reflect the booklet, while III contradicts its description of a religion-neutral code.
